name: MindCare AI — Agentic Mental Health Platform
tagline: Flagship AI project — Custom Adaptive Runtime with Planner, Hybrid RAG, Memory, MCP, and Evaluation
purpose: A production-grade agentic AI platform for mental health support — featuring a custom AI runtime engine built without LangChain, with planner-driven capability routing, hybrid RAG, conversation memory, and an evaluation framework.
problem_solved: Most mental health chatbots are shallow, generic, and unreliable. MindCare AI provides structured, empathetic, context-aware support powered by a production-grade AI runtime with measurable quality controls.
why_flagship: MindCare AI is Adarsh's most architecturally sophisticated project. It demonstrates deep AI systems engineering — not just API integration. It was built entirely without LangChain, using a custom runtime that mirrors enterprise AI system design patterns.

components.adaptive_runtime: Custom-built AI runtime engine — the core of MindCare AI. Manages the full pipeline from intent detection to streaming response without LangChain dependency.
components.planner: Intent classifier that categorizes user queries into capability types — crisis detection, mood tracking, therapy, journaling, resources, general support.
components.capability_layer: Modular capability system — each mental health function (crisis support, CBT exercises, mood journal, breathing techniques) is a separate capability module.
components.hybrid_rag: Combined keyword (BM25) + semantic (ChromaDB vector) retrieval. Hybrid approach outperforms pure semantic search by 23% on precision for mental health knowledge retrieval.
components.memory: Multi-layer memory — session buffer (short-term) + persistent user history (long-term). Enables contextual follow-up across sessions.
components.mcp: Model Context Protocol implementation — standardized interface for capability communication. Enables capability hot-swapping without system restart.
components.evaluator: Response quality evaluation framework — scores responses on accuracy, empathy, safety, and relevance. Filters low-quality responses before delivery.
components.llm_router: Multi-provider LLM router — selects optimal model (Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq) based on query complexity and latency requirements.

key_design_choices: No LangChain — full custom runtime for maximum control and performance
Hybrid RAG over pure semantic search for higher precision
MCP protocol for standardized capability interfaces
Evaluator as quality gate before every response delivery

key_achievements: Full custom AI runtime built without LangChain
Hybrid RAG (keyword + semantic) with 23% precision improvement over pure semantic
MCP (Model Context Protocol) implementation for capability standardization
Response quality evaluator with safety filtering

engineering_decisions.reason: LangChain is a black box. Building a custom runtime gives full control over latency, error handling, capability routing, and memory management. The custom runtime is also reusable — Adarsh reused the same planner-capability pattern in his portfolio AI assistant.

engineering_decisions.decision: Why Hybrid RAG over pure semantic?
engineering_decisions.reason: Pure semantic search misses exact keyword matches (medication names, specific techniques). BM25 keyword search is fast and precise for exact terms. Hybrid combines both: semantic for conceptual similarity + keyword for exact matches. Result: 23% higher precision.

Model Context Protocol standardizes how capabilities communicate with the runtime. This enables capability hot-swapping, testing, and extension without modifying core runtime logic. Follows the Open-Closed Principle.

In mental health AI, response quality and safety are non-negotiable. The evaluator acts as a quality gate — scoring every response before delivery. Low-scoring responses trigger fallback or regeneration. This prevents harmful outputs.

challenges: Building a reliable planner that correctly identifies crisis situations — solved with multi-signal classification and conservative thresholds
Balancing response quality with latency — solved with LLM routing (fast models for simple queries, capable models for complex ones)
Memory retrieval relevance — solved with hybrid memory search combining recency + relevance scoring
